hero_text: I build tools that solve real problems, from small scripts to apps that people use. I'm looking for a graduation internship from February 2027.

about_title: Clean code, calm structure, and just enough surprise.
about_text: I build websites that feel considered from the first glance to the last interaction. I care about readable code, responsive behavior, and design that does not feel generic.
principle_1_text: Interfaces should be easy to scan, and the code behind them should be easy to maintain.
principle_2_text: Every section, color, and interaction should earn its place instead of filling space.
principle_3_text: A portfolio can stay professional without feeling sterile. A small surprise makes it human.
project_1_text: My first project that friends use too. A Windows app that reads the game screen with OpenCV and EasyOCR and plays the game on its own. Because other people run it, it had to be properly finished: versioning, releases with an installer through GitHub Actions, and an interface in Dutch and English.
project_2_text: Turns a YouTube video or audio file into a clean transcript with timestamps, to read back yourself or to use as context for an AI. If the video has captions it uses those, otherwise it downloads the audio and transcribes it locally with Whisper on the GPU. Works from the command line and as an MCP server, so you can use it in your own AI tool.
project_3_text: A Selenium script that fills in the Wizard101 daily trivia quizzes for several accounts. It reads the questions from the HTML, looks the answer up in its own answer bank and logs unknown questions, so the bank keeps growing. It runs invisibly on a separate Windows desktop, so it never gets in my way.
